# Setup: Before you begin {.unnumbered}

::: callout-note
This page is the starting point for running the tutorials yourself. It tells you what software to install, how to install **all** R packages used across the book in one step, and how the datasets are organized so the code runs end-to-end on a fresh machine.
:::

## Software

-   **R** (version 4.2.0 or newer recommended). Download from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/).
-   **RStudio Desktop** (recommended IDE). Download from [posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
-   The book itself is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) (bundled with recent RStudio). You only need Quarto if you want to *render* the book; you do **not** need it to run the individual tutorial code.

## Installing all R packages in one step

Every package used anywhere in this book is listed in a single script, [`packages.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/EpiMethods/blob/main/packages.R), in the repository root. It installs the CRAN packages and the few GitHub-only packages (including `simcausal`, `WeightedROC`, and `svyTable1`).

From a fresh R session, run:

``` r
# from the root of a local clone of the EpiMethods repository
source("packages.R")
```

or, to run it directly from GitHub without cloning:

``` r
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ehsanx/EpiMethods/main/packages.R")
```

::: callout-important
**GitHub-only packages.** A few packages are not on CRAN and are installed from GitHub by `packages.R` via `remotes::install_github()`:

-   [`svyTable1`](https://github.com/ehsanx/svyTable1) — survey-aware Table 1 / reporting toolkit, used in several survey, confounding, and missing-data chapters.
-   [`simcausal`](https://github.com/osofr/simcausal) — DAG-based data simulation, used in the Simulation and Causal Roles modules.
-   [`WeightedROC`](https://github.com/tdhock/WeightedROC) — weighted ROC/AUC, used in the survey and missing-data modules.

Installing GitHub packages requires the `remotes` package (handled automatically) and, for some packages, a working compiler toolchain (Rtools on Windows, Xcode command-line tools on macOS).
:::

## Datasets and data access

Processed analytic datasets used by the tutorials are committed in the [`Data/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/EpiMethods/tree/main/Data) folder of the repository, organized by module (e.g., `Data/wrangling/`, `Data/propensityscore/`). Each chapter's **Overview** page links to the relevant data folder.

-   **NHANES** (US CDC) data are publicly available; the relevant cycles are either pre-processed in `Data/` or downloaded in-tutorial via the `nhanesA`/`NHANES` packages.
-   **CCHS** (Statistics Canada) microdata are not openly redistributable. The book ships the *processed* analytic objects needed to run the code; reproducing them from raw CCHS files requires institutional (e.g., UBC) access via the [Canadian Research Data Centre Network](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/microdata/data-centres) / UBC Abacus.

::: callout-tip
**Reproducibility standard.** The analyses are intended to run end-to-end by another analyst on a fresh machine after `source("packages.R")` and obtaining the committed `Data/` folder. Paths in the code are case-sensitive on Linux/macOS; keep the `Data/` folder name capitalized exactly as in the repository.
:::
